title: Multifunctional titanium–organic hybrid nanofibers for high-efficiency PM 2.5  filtration and photodynamic air disinfection
content: The development of air filtration materials that combine high particulate removal efficiency, antimicrobial functionality, and environmental stability remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report the fabrication of multifunctional electrospun nanofibrous membranes based on titanium alkoxide-modified polyvinylpyrrolidone (Ti–PVP), incorporating the photosensitizer crystal violet (CV). The incorporation of titanium alkoxide into the PVP matrix was associated with a transition from an intrinsically hydrophilic membrane (water contact angle ∼36°) to a hydrophobic membrane (contact angle >100°), significantly enhancing its moisture resistance and preserving its structural integrity under humid and water-exposure conditions. The incorporation of CV enabled photodynamically driven antimicrobial activity via reactive oxygen species generation under light irradiation. The optimized nanofibrous membranes exhibited excellent PM2.5 filtration performance, achieving ∼95% efficiency at an ultralow basis weight (0.5 mg cm−2) and up to 99% efficiency with a slight increase in loading while maintaining low airflow resistance. Furthermore, the membranes demonstrated sustained structural stability and filtration performance over extended operation. This work presents an effective strategy for designing durable, hydrophobic, and self-disinfecting nanofibrous air filters with strong potential for advanced air purification applications.
